STAT-F1 — Pairing changes the analysis unit, not causal identification
output.text:
## STAT-F1 — Pairing changes the analysis unit, not causal identification

Pairing means that each observation has a meaningful counterpart, for example two measurements on the same participant. For a paired mean comparison, take one difference per pair in a consistent direction: twenty people measured twice provide twenty differences, not forty independent observations. Uncertainty uses variation among those differences and the number of pairs. Dependence within a pair is expected; independence between pairs and the adequacy of the differences for the chosen method still need assessment. Repeating readings does not create independent participants. [psychology:S104]

An unpaired mean comparison instead concerns two groups without that correspondence, with uncertainty reflecting both groups and appropriate independence/distribution checks. Choose the method from the design; selecting whichever produces a smaller p-value changes the question. A pre/post difference describes change, while pairing handles dependence. It does not supply an untreated comparison or random assignment: time and other influences remain alternative explanations. The causal limit combines this selected reading with the earlier design sections. [psychology:S104]

**Original invented arithmetic:** four fictional puzzle times change from [40,55,70,85] to [38,52,69,79] seconds. Second minus first gives [-2,-3,-1,-6], with descriptive mean -3 seconds over four pairs. No p-value, interval, distributional adequacy or treatment effect is inferred. Practice is a possible explanation, not an established cause.

**Actual additional reading:** Diez, Çetinkaya-Rundel and Barr, *OpenIntro Statistics*, fourth edition, screen-reader copy updated2022-10-21, pp295–297 and301:7.2/7.2.1, selected7.2.2 opening/calculation and7.3/7.3.1 opening. These four pages are not the full sections or a repeated-measures/causal-inference course. Exact file licence and current provider terms were checked. The source textbook is [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/); these are original factual notes and invented data, with no copied source example, figure or exercise. Clustering, serial correlation, missing pairs, crossover designs and clinical interpretation need further evidence.

output.heading: F2 — Does a small p-value prove an important effect?
heading_path: Studied questions: foundations and broad health
F2 — Does a small p-value prove an important effect?
output.text:
## F2 — Does a small p-value prove an important effect?

**Scope:** statistical interpretation; no clinical treatment verdict follows from this card alone.

A p-value is computed under a specified null model. It describes how unusual the selected statistic, or results at least as extreme in the specified test direction, would be if that model applied. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true, that an intervention works, or that a reported effect occurred 'by chance'. State the hypothesis and assumptions rather than converting a p-value into a personal probability. [psychology:S104]

Failing to reject a null hypothesis does not establish that it is true. A study may leave important effects unresolved. Conversely, a very small difference can become statistically detectable in a large sample without becoming practically important. Examine the effect estimate, uncertainty, comparator, outcome scale and time horizon before discussing benefit or harm. Recommendation strength is another judgment and is not a synonym for statistical significance. [psychology:S104]

A Type I error rejects a true null hypothesis; a Type II error fails to reject a false one. A chosen significance threshold controls one error under assumptions; it does not remove every risk of a wrong conclusion. The consequences of mistakes and study design matter. Do not change thresholds after seeing a result to manufacture a favorable conclusion. That last instruction is this project's appraisal safeguard, not a reproduced textbook procedure.

**Original synthetic illustration:** two invented reports have the same small p-value but use different outcomes and report very different effect magnitudes. Their practical value need not be the same. A large p-value with a wide interval also cannot establish 'no meaningful difference'; this packet did not study equivalence/noninferiority methods. Do not claim that another test proves an exactly zero effect: meaningful bounds and exact equality are different claims.

**Reading:** OpenIntro 4e screen-reader selected pp. 211–213, 216–218 and 223–224: hypothesis framework, decision-error definitions, opening p-value definition and statistical versus practical significance. PDF pp. 218 and 224 visually checked. Full calculation exercises, multiplicity, equivalence and complete test-method appraisal were not completed. [psychology:S104]

output.heading: Identity, action and evidence
heading_path: Medicines, classes and treatment decisions
Identity, action and evidence
output.text:
## Identity, action and evidence

Identify INN, every active ingredient, brand, country, strength/concentration, form, release type and route. A brand can denote different combinations across countries. Liquid millilitres are not milligrams; metered and delivered inhaler amounts may differ. An injection, topical product and tablet with the same ingredient can have different approved uses and hazards. Preserve unknown identity instead of guessing from an unclear spoken name.

WHO ATC provides an anatomical, therapeutic and chemical hierarchy. Defined daily doses measure utilization, not a patient's prescribed dose. ATC membership does not establish equivalent potency, interchangeable indications or benefit. Search INN/class; trademarks and every combination ingredient are not necessarily searchable. WHO Essential Medicines Lists prioritize population needs; they are neither every effective medicine nor universal patient plans. Adult and child lists differ. Approval, national reimbursement, registration and actual pharmacy stock are separate facts. S298 S299

Separate mechanism, pharmacokinetics, outcomes, authorization and guideline position. Blocking a receptor explains biological action, not necessarily better survival or function. A biomarker response may be useful but is not automatically evidence of improved patient outcomes. Conditional recommendations may depend on severity, prior failures, biomarkers, contraindications, affordability and preferences. Evidence for one indication cannot establish another.

Use the national regulator first: Serbia ALIMS search and current SmPC/PIL; Russia current GRLS product entry and instructions. These are routes, not assertions that any specific product was retrieved or stocked. Failed retrieval requires disclosure and a pharmacist's current leaflet, not silent substitution of an old PDF. EMA covers centrally evaluated medicines; national registers cover others. Drugs@FDA establishes approval histories and approved labels; DailyMed provides submitted in-use labeling and includes products that are not approved medicines. A listing is not approval proof. S12 S300 S301 S302 S303

Read indication, contraindications, warnings, interactions, adverse effects, administration/formulation instructions, monitoring, missed-dose advice and life-stage/organ-function sections. SmPC sections commonly include 4.1, 4.3-4.8 and 5.2; verify document structure. Check revision date and manufacturer. Read guideline population, exceptions and evidence date. A contraindication, monitoring need and theoretical mechanism are different findings.

contexts.request: Как отличить статистическую значимость от полезного для пациента эффекта? Найди подходящие знания в плагине и укажи ограничения.
contexts.response:
В плагине есть карточка F2 о p-value и практической значимости, а также памятка Evidence appraisal methods. Малое p-value показывает несовместимость наблюдения с заданной нулевой моделью при её предпосылках. Оно не означает, что лечение полезно, и не является вероятностью истинности гипотезы. В большой выборке даже очень маленькое различие может стать статистически значимым.

Для оценки пользы смотрят на величину эффекта и её неопределённость, абсолютные изменения с учётом исходного риска, сравнение, срок наблюдения и важность исхода для пациента. Изменение биомаркера само по себе не доказывает улучшения здоровья; учитывают также вред и применимость исследования.

Ограничения: это общие заметки, а не оценка конкретного лечения. По записи плагина прочитаны лишь выбранные страницы OpenIntro, включая 211–213, 216–218 и 223–224; методы эквивалентности и не меньшей эффективности здесь не изучены. Большое p-value с широким интервалом не доказывает отсутствия полезного эффекта. Внешний первоисточник сейчас не открывался; поиск не проводит новую оценку доказательств.

output.heading: F2 — Does a small p-value prove an important effect?
heading_path: Studied questions: foundations and broad health
F2 — Does a small p-value prove an important effect?
output.text:
## F2 — Does a small p-value prove an important effect?

**Scope:** statistical interpretation; no clinical treatment verdict follows from this card alone.

A p-value is computed under a specified null model. It describes how unusual the selected statistic, or results at least as extreme in the specified test direction, would be if that model applied. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true, that an intervention works, or that a reported effect occurred 'by chance'. State the hypothesis and assumptions rather than converting a p-value into a personal probability. [psychology:S104]

Failing to reject a null hypothesis does not establish that it is true. A study may leave important effects unresolved. Conversely, a very small difference can become statistically detectable in a large sample without becoming practically important. Examine the effect estimate, uncertainty, comparator, outcome scale and time horizon before discussing benefit or harm. Recommendation strength is another judgment and is not a synonym for statistical significance. [psychology:S104]

A Type I error rejects a true null hypothesis; a Type II error fails to reject a false one. A chosen significance threshold controls one error under assumptions; it does not remove every risk of a wrong conclusion. The consequences of mistakes and study design matter. Do not change thresholds after seeing a result to manufacture a favorable conclusion. That last instruction is this project's appraisal safeguard, not a reproduced textbook procedure.

**Original synthetic illustration:** two invented reports have the same small p-value but use different outcomes and report very different effect magnitudes. Their practical value need not be the same. A large p-value with a wide interval also cannot establish 'no meaningful difference'; this packet did not study equivalence/noninferiority methods. Do not claim that another test proves an exactly zero effect: meaningful bounds and exact equality are different claims.

**Reading:** OpenIntro 4e screen-reader selected pp. 211–213, 216–218 and 223–224: hypothesis framework, decision-error definitions, opening p-value definition and statistical versus practical significance. PDF pp. 218 and 224 visually checked. Full calculation exercises, multiplicity, equivalence and complete test-method appraisal were not completed. [psychology:S104]

output.heading: Evidence appraisal methods
heading_path: Evidence appraisal methods
output.text:
# Evidence appraisal methods

Frame population, intervention, comparator and outcomes. Start with applicable current guidelines, then systematic reviews and primary research for unresolved questions. Distinguish recommendations, evidence and interpretation.

Record design, sample, baseline risk, comparator, follow-up, patient-relevant outcomes, absolute/relative effects, intervals, missing data, bias, funding and applicability. Mechanisms, surrogates, uncontrolled reports, vendor benchmarks and trial registration do not establish clinical benefit.

Randomized evidence can support many efficacy questions; observational studies can inform rare harms with confounding limits. Evidence level does not resolve a population mismatch. Do not combine incompatible endpoints or invent numbers from qualitative abstracts.
